model.rationale: The fundamentals all point one way: a D+10 seat, an incumbent with $2.6 million banked, and a challenger who has raised roughly four thousand dollars with no outside help. Markets at 96% for the Democratic side corroborate a double-digit expected margin.
model.watch: A last-minute wave of outside spending for Cohen combined with sharply lower Democratic turnout in this low-attention November race would be the main path to narrowing the margin.

overview:
California's 50th District leans Democratic by about ten points, and incumbent Scott Peters is seeking another term with roughly $2.6 million in the bank. His Republican opponent, Steve Cohen, has raised about four thousand dollars with no outside support, leaving him without the resources to run a competitive campaign. No public general-election polls are available for this race.

Prediction markets put the Democratic side's chances near 96 percent, and the underlying fundamentals — district lean, incumbency, and the fundraising gap — all point to a double-digit Democratic margin. The expectation is a comfortable win for Peters, with turnout in a low-salience race the main source of uncertainty. A Republican upset would require a simultaneous failure of both the fundamentals and the money picture.
